Title: Timely AUSAID interventions impact Gilgit-Baltistan schools
NewsSummary: Singal would have remained just another unheard, unseen idyllic town of Gilgit-Baltistan, if it were not for its middle schools making their mark across its home Ghizer district.

content.text: Singal would have remained just another unheard, unseen idyllic town of Gilgit-Baltistan, if it were not for its middle schools making their mark across its home Ghizer district. This year, the top four positions in the public Middle/Primary Standard Annual Examination 2014 at district Ghizer level have been clinched by two schools of Singal, both of whom are collaborators of a secondary school, a learning resource school, run by the Institute for Educational Development's Professional Development Centre, North. While not a single student failed in the recent examination, the LRS itself had bagged the top three positions in the Middle/Primary Standard Annual Examination 2013.

LRS Kashrote, a government girls secondary school in Gilgit, obtained the top two positions (as well as the top 5th position) at district level in the Middle/Primary Standard Annual Examination 2014. Government Primary School Takia, Chilas, a feeding school of LRS Chilas, obtained the top three positions in class 5th at the district level in the Middle/Primary Standard Annual Examination 2014.

These schools are part of the Education Development and Improvement Programme in Gilgit-Baltistan funded by AusAID - Australian Agency for International Development to improve the quality of education in seven districts across the region. And as this year's examination results sink in, it is evident that EDIP has made a difference for good.

Since 2010, a consortium of seven partners has implemented EDIP in 98 schools, of which over 70 per cent are government schools. Each cluster consists of four schools, a hub - a secondary school dubbed a Learning Resource School - and feeding units, which include primary/middle and sometimes high schools. A Professional Development Teacher or Teacher Educator is placed to lead the school improvement initiative in each cluster.

It is worth mentioning, that EDIP is capitalising on PDCN's successful Whole School Improvement Programme model that builds the capacity of all stakeholders be they teachers, school managers, parents, government officials and others.
